summary: Camden County steel fire tower on four acres: bought 1939, built 1942, relocated 1973, sold and dismantled for a buyer's farm in 2008 per one record.

facts.status_note: Record says the tower was dismantled in 2008 and moved to a buyer's farm, where it would be erected; no source confirms that it was

events.note: four acres acquired to erect a fire tower
one 68-foot steel tower listed among that year's construction
1951 newspaper describes the tower as used by the Commission as a fire lookout
fire tower relocated and a privy built at the site (FY1973-74)
sold to a private party; dismantled and moved to the buyer's farm

evidence.supports: four acres acquired in 1939 for a fire tower
evidence.quote: Four acres were acquired by the Conservation Commission for the purpose of erecting a fire tower.

evidence.supports: the 1942 annual report lists one 68-foot steel tower

evidence.quote: Hurricane Deck forestry tower right beside Highway 5 a dozen or so miles south of Gravois Mills.

evidence.quote: The tall tower is used as a lookout by the conservation commission for forest fires.

corrections.why: The record says the tower was dismantled and moved to a buyer's farm in 2008, so the structure may still exist elsewhere even though it is gone from the site.

notes_for_editor: Every fact here comes from one compiled record page that quotes Missouri Conservation Commission annual reports, the 1945-46 state manual and a 1951 Jefferson City newspaper. The January 2008 sale, dismantling and move rest on that page alone; two web searches found no independent confirmation. The page gives no removal of the tower from the lake-side site beyond the 2008 entry, and no source describes the site today. The brief coordinates (38.17847, -92.7972) could not be checked against a survey datasheet; no NGS record was found for this tower. Height is converted from 68 feet.
